extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for USPTO examiners on when and how to make nonstatutory double patenting (NSDP) rejections, including provisional rejections, §121 prohibitions, drafting requirements, and how applicants may overcome NSDP rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard for NSDP
rubrics_metrics.description: "A nonstatutory double patenting rejection is appropriate where the conflicting claims are not identical, but at least one examined application claim is not patentably distinct from the reference claim(s) because the examined application claim is either anticipated by, or would have been obvious over, the reference claim(s)." (MPEP 804, part (II)(B)(2))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference need not qualify as prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102. NSDP obviousness analysis is similar to, but not necessarily the same as, a §103 analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: When a reference qualifies for NSDP consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: Before making an NSDP rejection, confirm that the examined application and the reference patent/copending application: have at least one common joint inventor OR have at least one common applicant OR are commonly assigned/owned OR are non-commonly assigned/owned but deemed commonly owned based on a joint research agreement (35 U.S.C. 102(c) / pre-AIA 103(c)(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exception: a divisional filed as a result of a restriction requirement containing only claims consonant with the restriction cannot be used as an NSDP reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider all related patents/applications (benefit chain/continuity map/parallel families)
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners must consider patents and copending applications in the examined application's benefit chain, continuity map, and parallel families when assessing NSDP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make all available proper NSDP rejections in every application to protect the public; do not assume a single NSDP over one reference suffices. Conduct a full inventor/applicant/assignee search each time the application comes up for action because children and additional families may have been filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: NSDP across statutory categories
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no per se prohibition on making NSDP rejections across statutory categories (e.g., composition vs. method claims).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider NSDP where different statutory categories claim related subject matter (e.g., agent vs. method of using agent). See MPEP 804.

rubrics_metrics.name: NSDP based on anticipation (one-way genus-species test)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the reference claims, when properly construed, provide coverage for an embodiment within the scope of the examined claims, the examined claims are anticipated by the reference claims and thus are patentably indistinct (a one-way test).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a claim under examination is generic to a species or sub‑genus claimed in a conflicting patent/application, explain that the species/sub‑genus anticipates the genus and that a patent to the genus would improperly extend exclusivity. Use FP 8.34/8.35 as appropriate. MPEP 804 (II)(B)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: NSDP based on obviousness (Graham analysis applied to reference claims)
rubrics_metrics.description: Obviousness-based NSDP uses only the claims of the reference patent/application as the basis, but the reference disclosure may be consulted to interpret those claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform the Graham v. Deere analysis: (A) scope/content of reference claim; (B) differences between reference claim and examined claim; (C) level of ordinary skill; (D) objective indicia of nonobviousness. Use appropriate FP paragraphs (8.36/8.37 for secondary references, 8.34/8.35 for no secondary refs). MPEP 804 (II)(B)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not use "shortcut" rationales — full analysis required
rubrics_metrics.description: NSDP rejections based on an obviousness analysis must carry out a full analysis for all examined claims; merely pointing out scope overlap or addressing all claims in a single sentence is generally insufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure each claim addressed has a reasoned Graham-type analysis; avoid one-line or conclusory rejections. See MPEP 804.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of secondary references in NSDP (permitted and encouraged)
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners are encouraged to rely on secondary references to properly establish obviousness in an NSDP rejection; the secondary reference must qualify as prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraphs FP 8.36 and 8.37 for provisional and nonprovisional NSDP rejections with secondary references. See MPEP 804.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consulting the reference specification
rubrics_metrics.description: The reference's specification can be used as a dictionary to interpret the reference's claims and to confirm the scope of those claims when making an NSDP rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite and explain how the specification construes the reference claim; use FP 8.34/8.35/8.36/8.37 as appropriate. MPEP 804(II)(B)(2)(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Genus/species: immediately envisage test
rubrics_metrics.description: First determine whether a PHOSITA can immediately envisage the species from the genus claimed in the reference without consulting the reference specification; if yes, the genus anticipates the species.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not immediately envisaged, search for a secondary reference that would render the species obvious over the genus and explain motivation/expectation of success. If no secondary reference, consider whether the species is obvious over the genus using the reference's own disclosures (or consider equitable principles if not obvious). Use FP 8.33 and appropriate FP 8.34/8.35/8.36/8.37; rare equitable rejections use FP 8.38/8.39 with supervisory approval. See MPEP 804 (II)(B)(1) & (2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional NSDP rejections — when allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisional NSDP rejections may be made between two copending applications (not between an examined application and a patent). They may be over published or unpublished applications and over withdrawn claims in the copending application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A copending application used as provisional NSDP reference must be filed by the same inventive entity, have a common joint inventor/common applicant/common owner/assignee, or be by parties to a qualifying joint research agreement. Provisional NSDP stays provisional until the reference issues as a patent; note status changes in subsequent Office actions. MPEP 804 part (I)(B).

rubrics_metrics.name: When to withdraw a provisional NSDP rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: A provisional NSDP rejection is only withdrawn when the application is otherwise allowable and is the earlier-filed application (effective U.S. filing date determines earlier application).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use MPEP 804(I)(B)(1)(b)(i) and 1490 part (VI)(D)(1) to determine earlier effective U.S. filing dates; maintain or withdraw provisional rejections per the filing-date relationships (table provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional NSDP over withdrawn reference claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Withdrawn claims in a copending application may be used as reference claims for a provisional NSDP rejection in the examined application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not reject withdrawn claims in the examined application for NSDP. Include the withdrawn claim(s) of the copending application as reference claims in the provisional rejection. MPEP 804 (II)(B)(1); 2144.08.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional NSDP over unpublished applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisional NSDP rejections can be raised before the reference copending application is published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not wait for publication to make provisional NSDP rejections. MPEP 804 part (I)(B).

rubrics_metrics.name: Make all available proper NSDP rejections (do not assume single TD covers all)
rubrics_metrics.description: All available proper NSDP rejections must be made in every application — writing an NSDP over one patent does not relieve the examiner of considering other related patents/applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because patents may have differing expiration dates due to patent term adjustment and because parallel families/related applications may exist, consider NSDP over all relevant references in the benefit chain, continuity map, and parallel families.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 121 prohibition — when NSDP is statutorily barred
rubrics_metrics.description: The third sentence of 35 U.S.C. 121 prohibits using a patent that issued on an application (or a divisional filed as a result of a restriction requirement) as a reference against a divisional or the original application if the divisional was filed before issuance of the other patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: First determine whether an NSDP rejection (anticipation/obviousness) is available; then assess whether §121 applies by checking for restriction requirements in the related applications, whether any restriction/election was withdrawn, and whether the examined invention/species is a nonelected invention consonant with the restriction. If §121 applies, NSDP is not available. See MPEP 804.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: §121 applicability — look to filing/parent chain and restriction history
rubrics_metrics.description: To assess §121, examine all related applications in the benefit chain for restriction requirements, whether elections were made, and whether restrictions were withdrawn; determine if the examined invention is a nonelected invention or species consonant with the restriction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If restriction/election existed and the examined invention was a nonelected species filed as a divisional as a result of that restriction, §121 may bar NSDP. If no restriction was made in the parent(s), §121 does not apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: §121 does not apply to voluntary divisionals or absent restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: 35 U.S.C. 121's prohibition only applies when a divisional application is filed as a result of a restriction requirement; voluntary divisional filings or situations with no restriction do not create the §121 bar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume mere status as a divisional prevents NSDP; verify restriction history. See MPEP 804.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: §121 applies to species elections and grouped inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: The §121 prohibition applies to restrictions based on grouped inventions and elections of species (e.g., a species election within a Markush/genus election).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant elected one species and canceled others, patents claiming the elected species cannot be used for NSDP against divisional claims to nonelected species; recognize the potential for many divisional filings and apply §121 accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: NSDP based on equitable principles (improper timewise extension)
rubrics_metrics.description: NSDP can be based on equitable principles to prevent an unjustified timewise extension of patent rights (rare). Examples include In re Schneller and Geneva v. GlaxoSmithKline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such rejections are rare and require Supervisory Patent Examiner approval and Technology Center Director signature. Use FP 8.38 (issued patent vs application) or FP 8.39 (provisional) and contact a double-patenting POC. Explain factual basis thoroughly.

rubrics_metrics.name: NSDP and overlapping §103 art rejections — both may be required
rubrics_metrics.description: Even if the examiner makes a compliant §103 rejection over a prior-art reference, an NSDP rejection must still be made if the NSDP analysis over the claims of a patent/application in view of that prior art shows patentable indistinctness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not omit an NSDP rejection simply because a §103 rejection exists; NSDP addresses other policy concerns (timewise extension/multiple suits).

rubrics_metrics.name: Drafting proper NSDP rejections — form paragraphs and explanations
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the appropriate form paragraphs and include claim-by-claim reasoning: FP 8.33 (general), 8.34/8.35 (no secondary references), 8.36/8.37 (with secondary references / provisional language), 8.38/8.39 (equitable principles).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the rejection explains why each examined claim is patentably indistinct from each reference claim relied upon, performing the necessary Graham-type analysis for obviousness-based rejections or an anticipation explanation for anticipation-based rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overcoming NSDP rejections — applicant options
rubrics_metrics.description: To overcome an NSDP rejection based on anticipation: (A) amend the examined claims so reference claims no longer anticipate, (B) cancel the relevant reference claims, or (C) obtain an approved terminal disclaimer in the examined application. Evidence of secondary considerations is NOT an option for anticipation-based NSDP; a promise to file a TD later is NOT an option.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For obviousness-based NSDP, options include claim amendment, cancellation, evidence of unexpected results (if properly presented), or an approved TD in the examined application. A TD is not effective until approved and only effective in the application in which it is filed. Examiners should confirm reference numbers on TDs but need not review TD compliance; contact Patent Legal Research Center if TD approval is unclear. See MPEP 804, 804.02.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminal disclaimer rules and effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: A terminal disclaimer (TD) is not effective to overcome an NSDP rejection until approved; a TD filed in the reference application does not obviate the need to file a TD in the examined application—the TD only affects the application in which it was filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should not assume a filed but unapproved TD overcomes an NSDP rejection. Confirm approved TDs via file history or contact Patent Legal Research Center. Use MPEP 804.02 for guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Changing application status (CON to DIV) and impact on NSDP
rubrics_metrics.description: If the most recent filing receipt identifies an application as a divisional (DIV) rather than a continuation (CON), examiners should treat the filing receipt as the USPTO's information of record; a corrected filing receipt may change whether §121 applies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners need not evaluate a corrected ADS before dropping an NSDP rejection; rely on the most recent filing receipt (document code: APP.FILE.REC). Do not act inconsistently with the most recent filing receipt. See MPEP 211.02(a); 503; 601.05(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Earlier-filed/earlier-issued patents do not automatically preclude NSDP
rubrics_metrics.description: Even if a patent was filed before the examined application, NSDP over that patent may still be available because NSDP addresses more than improper timewise extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not speculate about patent term expiration dates (PTA calculations are complex). A TD filed in the examined application ties enforceability to common ownership and provides public notice; consider NSDP regardless of filing order where appropriate. See MPEP 804.02.
